speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I'm Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you describe exactly what it looks like and how it feels? When did this rash first appear, and have you noticed any similar issues elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Atopic Dermatitis. While the family history of psoriasis is noted, the clinical presentation of a red, scaly rash on a 3-month-old infant that flares in cold weather is most consistent with infantile eczema. I am ready to finalize the diagnosis once you confirm if there is a family history of atopy (asthma or hay fever) and if the rash is itchy.
